messages:
Alex: Quick update — I landed the kernel-prefork branch to staging and kicked off a smoke run. Throughput looks promising for short-seq workloads (~8x), but observed a 10-15% CPU spike on nvlink nodes.
Maya: Nice! Did you also include the kv-ttl eviction tweak from the draft? :eyes:
Alex: Not yet. I want to validate the canary first, then roll the kv tweak in. Plan: canary 10% with kernel-prefork + kv-prefetch flag off initially.
infra-bot: Canary deployment started (canary_id=canary-1758888-1) :rocket:
Raul: FYI: on canary traffic I'm seeing p99 for long-context requests jump from ~120ms to ~190ms. Logs show a lot of fallback events on cache path.
Maya: Can you paste the log tail? Suspect remote fallback or disk reads.
Raul: ```WARN runtime.kvcache: miss -> fallback(backend=remote) ctx=abcd1234
DEBUG runtime.kv: kv_get_batch durations: median=1.8ms warm, 88ms cold, outliers=300ms+```
Alex: That matches the CPU spikes. If cache miss rate is high, prefetch could help. I can enable `--kv-prefetch=hot-only` on canary nodes and rerun.
Sarah: Notebook evals look good — model quality unchanged on the canary. No generation regressions.
PM-Jordan: Blocking dependency: infra needs to approve temporary egress increase for remote-kv during the canary window. @Luis can you approve?
Luis: Approving now; note we cap at 200MB/s for the week. I'll bump limits for the canary window and monitor.
Maya: I've opened PR #4873 to add finer-grained kv cache metrics (tags by shard/hotness). Alex, can you please review the metric name changes?
Alex: Looking now. Small nits but nothing blocking.
infra-bot: Canary traffic increased 5% -> 10% (timestamp=1758888920)
Raul: After toggling prefetch to hot-only on canary, p99 dropped to ~130ms. Better but not fully back to baseline. CPU flame shows hotspot in `kv_batch_exec` loop.
Maya: Can we run a short assembly-level profile on that kernel function? Might be inlined codegen causing stalls.
Alex: Yes — pairing ok? I can be on in ~45 minutes.
Maya: I can do 45.
PM-Jordan: Sprint goal recap: merge kernel-prefork to main, enable kv-prefetch default for hot-model set, and ship rollout + rollback runbook. Current blockers: kernel perf regression triage and final infra egress guardrails (which Luis handled).
Sarah: I'll add a dashboard card for p95/p99 and error rate; also add long-context evals so product can watch quality during rollout.
Maya: Also opened PR #4880 to temporarily raise eviction threshold for canary nodes if we see churn. Alex, can we scope it to the canary lamdbas only?
Luis: OK to apply for canary nodes. I'll coordinate limits with infra.
Alex: Plan: coordinate patch + rolling restart at 23:00 PST (quiet window). I'll post a checklist here before the restart.
Raul: I'll run a focused load test 30 minutes before restart and upload results to the thread.
Sarah: Thanks — ping here after restart with the metrics snapshot :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Alex: Thanks everyone. Quick call if needed after results come in.
